narrative.title: Pacing a Robotic Picker Before the Shift Ends
narrative.scenario: A warehouse robot must clear several part bins before the maintenance crew returns in h minutes. Each minute it works on one bin at a fixed pick rate; a smaller bin finishes early and the robot idles for the rest of that minute. Choose the slowest rate that still empties every bin in time.
narrative.inputFormat: An array piles of n positive integers and an integer h, the deadline in hours.
narrative.outputFormat: The minimum integer eating speed k such that all piles are finished within h hours.

complexity.optimalTime: O(n log M), where M is the largest pile

testCases.explanation: At rate 4 the bins take 1, 2, 2 and 3 minutes for a total of 8; rate 3 would need 9.
With only five minutes and five bins, one bin must go per minute, so the rate must cover the largest bin.

hintLevels: Level 1: Instead of searching the piles, search the rate - feasibility is monotonic in the rate.
Level 2: For a candidate rate, sum ceil(pile / rate) over all piles and compare against the deadline; search the rate range from 1 to the largest pile.
Level 3: A partially finished bin still consumes its own minute, so the per-bin cost is a ceiling division, and the deadline is guaranteed to be at least the bin count so an answer always exists.
